themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Tesla is reportedly readying parts for 15,000 Optimus units by year-end, ramping to 2,500/week — but every unit is routed to Tesla's own factories and an internal "Optimus Academy," not customers, and the Gen 3 reveal keeps slipping; Polymarket odds of a commercial launch by end-2026 have fallen to ~9% from ~33% a month ago. Figure AI countered on Sep 3 with a partnership with Nscale for up to 100,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs and an initial $3.5B compute commitment. Global H1 2026 humanoid shipments still surged ~272% YoY to 19,000-22,000 units — with Chinese makers holding ~93-97% of that volume.

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Symbotic hit a fresh 52-week low of $37.68 (Sep 1) and Barclays cut its price target again to $38 from $44 on Sep 8, reiterating Sell — even after last quarter's GAAP profitability and $721M revenue print. Shares have since clawed back to the low-$40s (~$42.72, Sep 11), leaving the stock caught between improving fundamentals and persistently bearish sell-side sentiment.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: Intuitive Surgical closed at $353.24 (Sep 9, ~$124.8B market cap) and reaffirmed its 13.5-15.5% full-year procedure-growth guidance at the Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference the same day. A new meta-analysis published Sep 8 found statistically significant outcome improvements for da Vinci surgery versus laparoscopic/open approaches across 13 common conditions. Consensus target sits at $508.68 (22 buy/8 hold/1 sell) — about 44% upside — even with the stock still down roughly a third YTD.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: AeroVironment beat on both lines in its Sep 9 Q1 FY27 report — revenue $480.5M vs. $459.9M est., EPS $0.59 vs. $0.30 est. — with a record $1.5B backlog (+37% YoY) and margins expanding to 40% from 36%; shares still fell ~5% before recovering after-hours. Kratos continues to carry a $2.08B backlog off its Sep 1 satcom-gateway award, with no fresh catalyst this week. Strong fundamentals and share performance remain decoupled across this sub-sector.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Caterpillar's FieldAI partnership (formalized Sep 5) pairs Cat's jobsite data with FieldAI's robot-agnostic foundation models, running on NVIDIA accelerated computing and Omniverse digital-twin tooling, for autonomous inspections and situational awareness. Deere continues rolling out autonomous mowers with vision-AI and RTK-GPS perception stacks. Both remain diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall return.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Fanuc has stabilized near ¥5,735 (Sep 11), essentially flat from ¥5,725 the prior week and still well off its ¥7,351 average target, though the 8-buy/1-sell consensus rating held. Yaskawa remains in the ¥4,500 area (Sep 3). Keyence continues trading near record highs in the ¥70,000-72,600 range with no fresh guidance this week.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: MP Materials launched "Project Swarm" this week, letting drone and motor manufacturers reserve rare-earth magnet capacity ahead of its upcoming $1.3B 10X facility in Northlake, TX — a second structural growth line on top of the NdPr volume surge and China supply-pause tailwind already driving the stock. Vishay Precision Group remains 2026's best-performing robotics supply-chain stock on booked humanoid-actuator orders.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA launched the Jetson Orin Nano 2 (late August) — an entry-level robotics computer with 2x the inference performance and 40% less power draw than its predecessor, with modules/dev kits due H1 2027 — with Cognex, Doosan Bobcat and Matic among the first adopters. The robotics developer base has now grown past 3M, up from 2M+ just weeks ago, with JetPack 7.2 and NemoClaw adding agentic-AI capability to the stack.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree's slump has extended into a third straight week, now compounded by the FCC's ban on foreign-made humanoid/quadruped imports — a policy set to be tested by Xi Jinping's planned September visit to meet President Trump. China's National Development and Reform Commission has separately warned of a domestic robotics bubble, flagging startups building near-identical machines. LimX Dynamics and Agibot continue scaling toward Hong Kong-area listings regardless.

Atlas fleets shipping to Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind, all 2026 production committed; Hyundai targets 2028 factory use at 30,000 units/year. Public exposure only via Hyundai (KRX: 005380).

private_watchlist.name: Agibot / LimX Dynamics
private_watchlist.note: LimX closed a $200M pre-IPO round ($2.2B / RMB 15B valuation) and is preparing a Hong Kong listing; Agibot continues scaling shipments. Chinese humanoid startups are increasingly racing toward IPOs, partly to reopen funding channels narrowed by US investment curbs and the FCC's import ban.

bear_case.title: Unitree's crash is now a three-week story
bear_case.description: Shares are down ~56% from their Aug 19 intraday peak as of Sep 11 — a third straight week of declines. China's own National Development and Reform Commission has now warned of a domestic robotics bubble, specifically flagging startups producing near-identical machines. This is no longer a hypothetical warning from outside observers — Beijing's own planning body is saying it too, even as the FCC's US import ban compounds the pressure.

bear_case.title: The market is pricing out Optimus's near-term case
bear_case.description: Polymarket odds of a commercial Tesla Optimus launch by end-2026 have fallen to ~9%, down from ~33% just a month earlier, as the Gen 3 reveal keeps slipping and Tesla routes early units to its own "Optimus Academy" rather than customers. When a prediction market this sharply reprices the nearest-term humanoid commercialization case, it's a signal the broader timeline enthusiasm may be running ahead of engineering reality.

bear_case.title: Humanoid funding still outruns humanoid revenue
bear_case.description: Dealroom puts 2026 robotics funding near $55.8B — nearly double last year's record, with PitchBook separately clocking $18.6B in Q2 2026 alone across 450 deals. Figure AI's $39B valuation already exceeds Goldman's full 2035 global humanoid TAM estimate of $38B, even before its new $3.5B Nscale compute commitment adds to the cash burn. Most of these companies still don't have revenue that justifies the price tag.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids, with Agibot alone now claiming 15,000 cumulative units shipped; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Beats don't protect the stock — but they can be a real signal
bear_case.description: Symbotic hit a fresh 52-week low (Sep 1) and Barclays cut its target again (to $38 from $44, Sep 8) despite GAAP profitability. AeroVironment beat decisively on Sep 9 — record backlog, expanding margins — and shares still fell ~5% on the day. In parts of this sector, sentiment is doing more work than headline numbers, which cuts both ways: it can mean an opportunity is being mispriced, or that the market knows something the print doesn't show yet.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures — and 150+ Chinese humanoid startups, now including BYD, are competing on price and scale even as Unitree's own stock struggles to hold its valuation and Beijing's planners flag the same crowding risk.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples ranged from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) in Q4 2025 — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.

positions.name: Vishay Precision Group
positions.note: Still 2026's best-performing robotics supply-chain name on booked humanoid-actuator orders, but small enough that customer concentration remains a real single-name risk.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: Reaffirmed FY guidance at the Wells Fargo conference and a new meta-analysis backed da Vinci's outcome edge across 13 conditions this week — genuine incremental positives, but shares are still down ~34% YTD on pace for the weakest year since 2008, so the valuation call still argues for waiting.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: Named a first-wave adopter of NVIDIA's new Jetson Orin Nano 2 — a incremental positive — but still digesting the earlier HSBC downgrade to Hold ($65 PT); not yet enough to justify moving off the sidelines.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: The FieldAI partnership was formalized Sep 5 with NVIDIA compute and Omniverse tooling attached, but robotics remains a rounding error next to the construction-cycle exposure you'd actually be buying.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Shares have merely stabilized near ¥5,735 (Sep 11) rather than recovered — still well off the ¥7,351 average target despite an intact 8-buy/1-sell rating.

positions.name: ABB Ltd
positions.note: Still awaiting regulatory clearance on the SoftBank robotics sale, with the division president set to depart by year-end — little left here to hold for ahead of a mid-to-late-2026 close.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: No fresh catalyst this week after last month's guidance cut to $9-10M for FY26; +404% YoY revenue growth still isn't outrunning the downward guidance revisions.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Every Optimus unit built this year is routed to Tesla's own 'Optimus Academy,' not customers, and the Gen 3 reveal keeps slipping. Polymarket odds of a commercial launch by end-2026 have collapsed to ~9% from ~33% a month ago — moved from Speculative to Avoid as the market itself is now pricing in the delay.

positions.name: Unitree
positions.note: Now down ~56% from its Aug 19 peak for a third straight week, with China's own NDRC warning of a domestic bubble on top of the FCC's US import ban — both price action and policy remain firmly against it.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: RPA is being disrupted by the same AI agents it claims to ride, and the robotics label is marketing rather than hardware.
